# Pressure-temperature flash with a convergence flag

`eos.pt_flash_check`

## Source

**Rachford, H. H.; Rice, J. D. (1952); Michelsen, M. L. (1982)**

The same procedure as `eos.pt_flash`, with the caller's tolerance and a non-throwing cap. NeqSim's `TPflash` is the source of the scheme; it has no public tolerance or convergence-flag setter, so the diagnostic contract is azoth's.

DOI: [10.1016/0378-3812(82)85001-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-3812(82)85001-2)


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `successive_substitution_flash` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-10` |
| Max iterations | `300` |
| Initialisation | `wilson` |

## Inner procedure

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `rachford_rice_bisection` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-14` |
| Max iterations | `200` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank with the keycard's overrides applied. |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature. |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure. |
| `z` | dimensionless | overall mole fractions. Checked rather than renormalised. |
| `tolerance` | dimensionless | *Optional.* the outer stopping tolerance; absent takes `algorithm.tolerance`, 1e-10. |
| `strict` | - | *Optional.* whether a cap raises; absent is true. False returns the last iterate with `converged = false`. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vapour_fraction` | dimensionless | *Optional.* The vapour fraction, in `[0, 1]` for a two-phase split; outside that it is the negative-flash value and the feed is single phase. Absent where there is genuinely no vapour fraction. |
| `x` | dimensionless | liquid-phase mole fractions |
| `y` | dimensionless | vapour-phase mole fractions |
| `k` | dimensionless | `K_i = y_i / x_i = phi_i^L / phi_i^V`. |
| `ln_phi_liquid` | dimensionless | fugacity coefficients in the liquid phase, as logarithms. |
| `ln_phi_vapour` | dimensionless | fugacity coefficients in the vapour phase, as logarithms. |
| `z_liquid` | dimensionless | the liquid root of the cubic at the liquid composition. |
| `z_vapour` | dimensionless | the vapour root at the vapour composition. |
| `min_t_over_tc` | dimensionless | the smallest `T / Tc_i` over the components. |
| `phase` | two_phase / all_liquid / all_vapour / trivial | What the state is: `two_phase`, `all_liquid`, `all_vapour`, or `trivial` (the iteration converged to `x = y = z`). |
| `converged` | - | whether the iteration met its tolerance, or settled on a trivial or single-phase state by proof. False only when `strict = false` and the loop hit its cap; the split is then the last iterate, not a converged state. |
| `iterations` | dimensionless | outer steps taken. |
| `residual` | dimensionless | the last step's convergence measure. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |
| `tolerance > 0` | raises | a stopping tolerance; zero can never be met and a negative value is not a distance |
| `min_t_over_tc <= 0.9` | warns `OUT_OF_VALID_RANGE` | Above `T / Tc = 0.9` for the nearest component the cubic's roots are close to coalescing and successive substitution converges slowly or to the trivial solution. |

## Assumptions

- **this is `eos.pt_flash` with the contract a time march needs.** It runs the same successive-substitution and second-order procedures, with the same Wilson start and trivial-solution test, and adds a caller-set tolerance and a non-throwing mode; the arithmetic is not a second flash.
- A component's `Tc`, `Pc`, `omega` and every `kij` come from the databank with the keycard's overrides applied, exactly as `eos.pt_flash` reads them.
- the equation of state is Peng-Robinson with the coefficient `eos.pr_kappa` computes, and the mixture fugacity coefficient is the one `eos.pt_flash` uses.
- `tolerance` overrides `algorithm.tolerance` for the outer stopping rule and the final acceptance; the fallback Newton keeps its own declared tolerance unless `tolerance` is supplied, in which case the supplied value is the acceptance for both.
- `strict` is true when absent. False turns the iteration cap into a result: the last iterate is returned with `converged = false` and a `SOLVER_NOT_CONVERGED` warning. A non-finite K-value still raises under either setting, because a diverged iteration is not a state.
- There is no stability test: a converged split is a stationary point of the flash equations, not a proof that the feed was unstable.

## How far this is checked
**`partially_verified`** — exercised against expectations pinned in its own spec, with no independent oracle recorded for it - **the normal case rather than a defect**.

- Tests: 2 declared, every one run
- External check: no external validation case names it

The same account travels with every result this returns: `result.provenance`
carries the status, the spec and both kernels with a SHA-256 of each, and which
declared checks *that call* could not evaluate.

## References

- Rachford, H. H.; Rice, J. D. (1952). "Procedure for Use of Electronic Digital Computers in Calculating Flash Vaporization Hydrocarbon Equilibrium." Journal of Petroleum Technology 4(10), 19-3. DOI 10.2118/952327-G
- Michelsen, M. L. (1982). "The isothermal flash problem. Part I. Stability." Fluid Phase Equilibria 9(1), 1-19. DOI 10.1016/0378-3812(82)85001-2.
- NeqSim master `thermodynamicoperations/flashops/TPflash.java`, whose outer loop has no tolerance setter and exits silently at its iteration cap; the convergence flag is azoth's contract, not a ported NeqSim API.
